- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced when historical prices are volatile or show recent downward trends — model reacts too slowly.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing short-term reversals — often misses sudden drops or spikes by 1–3 days.
- When true prices are near or below historical mean, model tends to overpredict — fails to recognize mean reversion.
- Model is prone to overfitting recent high prices — forecasts remain elevated even when true prices are declining.
